item.text: {"debateNumber":223,"decisions":[{"moveId":"pro-science-leaves-existential-questions","label":"Argument from ignorance","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Collins reports that science did not answer certain existential questions, but he does not treat that noncoverage as proof that God exists or that theology is true. The assessment expressly characterizes the conclusion as restrained and says the move establishes epistemic scope rather than a theistic inference. Its request for positive, publicly assessable reasons identifies a future burden, not a material ignorance inference already made.","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/argument-from-ignorance/","context":"Collins lists questions about purpose, death, God, and existence that his scientific competence was not helping him answer, describing himself as ill-equipped to approach them."},{"moveId":"pro-comparative-inquiry-supported-faith","label":"Appeal to authority","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Although Collins names C. S. Lewis as especially influential, he does not rely on Lewis's reputation or institutional status as settling Christianity's truth. He describes a prolonged process in which arguments changed his judgment. The assessment faults the absence of those arguments and comparative standards, making the defect nonreproducible underdevelopment rather than a material appeal to authority.","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/appeal-to-authority/","context":"Collins recounts two years of theological inquiry, says Lewis particularly influenced him, and reports eventually judging faith more rational than atheism."},{"moveId":"pro-comparative-inquiry-supported-faith","label":"Subjective validation","type":"bias","decision":"rejected","rationale":"The move is autobiographical testimony about what Collins came to believe after reflection; it does not assert that Christianity is accurate because it felt personally resonant or confirmed a private experience. The assessment calls the account sincere but publicly unevaluable because its premises are omitted. That missing public argument does not establish that personal meaningfulness was substituted for accuracy.","url":"https://cogbias.site/biases/subjective-validation/","context":"Collins describes his initial hostility, the revision of objections he came to regard as superficial, and his personal conclusion that faith was more rational."},{"moveId":"con-simple-to-complex-presupposition","label":"Belief bias","type":"bias","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Dawkins candidly discloses that evolutionary study makes simple-to-complex explanation attractive to him, but he does not judge a specified argument valid merely because its conclusion feels believable. The assessment treats the disclosure as transparent yet insufficiently defended and asks him to formulate a general explanatory principle. That is low warrant, not the defined substitution of plausibility for inferential validity.","url":"https://cogbias.site/biases/belief-bias/","context":"Dawkins acknowledges presuppositions on both sides and says he is 'in love with' explaining complex things in terms of simpler things."},{"moveId":"pro-science-cannot-prove-transcendent","label":"Special pleading","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Collins gives a relevant proposed reason for limiting science: its tools investigate nature, whereas the hypothesized God is extra-natural. That distinction may be contestable and risks insulating the hypothesis, but it is not an exception offered without a principle. The assessment identifies an unexplained confirmation-disconfirmation problem and demands evidential accountability; it does not establish that Collins has applied a wholly reasonless different standard.","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/special-pleading/","context":"Collins distinguishes scientific investigation of nature, indirect evidential considerations about God, and conclusive proof or disproof of an extra-natural being."},{"moveId":"pro-evolution-compatible-with-plan","label":"Argument from ignorance","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Collins argues only that evolutionary explanation does not logically exclude a deeper plan; he does not infer that a plan therefore exists. The assessment explicitly distinguishes compatibility from probability and says no independent warrant for an actual plan is supplied. That limitation is missing positive evidence, while the exact fallacy would require treating non-disproof itself as establishing the plan's truth.","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/argument-from-ignorance/","context":"Collins fully credits evolution's explanation of biological diversity while maintaining that its mechanism remains logically compatible with divine purpose at a deeper level."},{"moveId":"con-evolution-waste-and-redundancy","label":"Belief bias","type":"bias","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Dawkins's statement that he would design more directly rests on speculative expectations about divine preferences, but it does not evaluate an argument merely by whether its conclusion feels believable. The assessment separates that weak divine-psychology premise from the stronger redundancy claim and asks him to emphasize the latter. Speculation and insufficient warrant do not independently satisfy the catalog definition of belief bias.","url":"https://cogbias.site/biases/belief-bias/","context":"Dawkins calls natural selection wasteful for an intending creator and argues that its capacity to operate without God renders divine direction superfluous."},{"moveId":"pro-evolution-as-divine-means","label":"Confirmation bias","type":"bias","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Collins interprets evolution as elegant within his theological model, but the move does not show him seeking, selecting, remembering, or discounting evidence in a one-sided way. The assessment says the proposal fails to distinguish providential evolution from natural history and may reflect a prior interpretation. That evidential underdetermination is not enough to infer the defined selective treatment of evidence.","url":"https://cogbias.site/biases/confirmation-bias/","context":"Collins conditionally proposes that a timeless God could knowingly use evolution as an elegant means of producing conscious creatures without repeated intervention."},{"moveId":"pro-evolution-as-divine-means","label":"Subjective validation","type":"bias","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Calling the model 'amazing' and evolution 'elegant' expresses admiration, but Collins presents a conditional theological possibility rather than claiming that its personal appeal verifies its truth. The assessment criticizes unsupported foreknowledge, intention, and comparative plausibility and warns that elegance may reflect prior interpretation. It does not establish reliance on private resonance as evidence of accuracy.","url":"https://cogbias.site/biases/subjective-validation/","context":"Collins describes as amazing the possibility that an atemporal God intended conscious life and knew evolution's outcome while allowing stable processes to unfold."},{"moveId":"pro-timelessness-answers-duration","label":"Equivocation","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Referring to immense evolutionary time as a 'blink' for an atemporal God is conceptually awkward temporal imagery, but Collins does not shift a key term's meaning between premises and conclusion. The assessment identifies tension in describing timelessness and notes that other forms of waste remain unanswered. Neither point demonstrates an equivocation that materially strengthens the inference.","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/equivocation/","context":"Collins isolates evolution's elapsed duration and argues that it would not constitute delay or inconvenience from the perspective of a God outside time."},{"moveId":"pro-timelessness-answers-duration","label":"Special pleading","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Atemporality is offered as a category-based reason that elapsed temporal duration would not burden God as it burdens temporal agents. The premise requires independent defense and does not answer suffering, redundancy, or autonomous sufficiency, but those are limitations of scope and warrant. The assessment does not show an exception imposed without a principled reason, as the exact special-pleading definition requires.","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/special-pleading/","context":"Collins says evolution's long duration should not trouble a timeless God, for whom the completed process is not experienced as a prolonged wait."},{"moveId":"pro-laws-remain-unexplained","label":"Argument from ignorance","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Collins raises the residual question of where the physical laws enabling evolution came from but does not conclude in this move that God authored them merely because their origin remains unexplained. The assessment commends the distinction between levels of explanation and expressly says the residual question is not yet divine evidence. Its demand for a positive comparative argument confirms that the prohibited inference has not yet occurred.","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/argument-from-ignorance/","context":"After accepting the bottom-up evolutionary account, Collins asks Dawkins where the more fundamental physical laws on which that account depends originated."},{"moveId":"pro-transcendent-mind-exceeds-concepts","label":"Special pleading","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Collins gives a principled subject-matter distinction: ordinary models drawn from biological brains or engineered systems may inadequately describe a transcendent mind. The assessment warns that this could become asymmetric insulation if favorable claims remained admissible while complexity objections were excluded, but it does not find that full asymmetric practice in the move. A threatened future exception is not material special pleading already instantiated.","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/special-pleading/","context":"Collins argues that human attempts to imagine the nature and capabilities of a transcendent divine mind would be radically inadequate to their proposed object."},{"moveId":"con-divine-simplicity-implausible","label":"Begging the question","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Dawkins offers a substantive, though inadequately defended, premise that selecting fundamental constants requires corresponding informational or internal complexity. That bridge may assume an inappropriate complexity metric and fails to engage divine simplicity, but it is not simply the conclusion restated as a premise. The assessment identifies an unsupported capability-to-composition inference rather than circular reasoning.","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/begging-the-question/","context":"Dawkins rejects claims of divine simplicity on the ground that a being able to choose life-permitting physical constants must possess sophisticated discriminatory capacity."},{"moveId":"pro-multiverse-also-evidential-leap","label":"Ambiguity effect","type":"bias","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Collins emphasizes the multiverse's uncertainty and possible experimental inaccessibility, yet he explicitly recognizes its anthropic explanatory role and treats it as a serious competitor. The assessment faults his use of direct observability as an incomplete evidential comparison and notes possible indirect support from physics. It does not establish that ambiguity itself caused him to reject or irrationally disfavor the hypothesis.","url":"https://cogbias.site/biases/ambiguity-effect/","context":"Collins explains observer selection in an infinite multiverse but calls commitment to experimentally inaccessible universes an evidential leap comparable to theistic commitment."},{"moveId":"pro-timeless-god-stops-regress","label":"Special pleading","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Collins supplies atemporality as a relevant proposed difference between entities with temporal origins and a creator outside time. That distinction addresses only when God began, leaving explanatory dependence, intentions, and complexity unresolved, and it needs independent support. Nevertheless, the assessment recognizes it as an answer to the temporal regress; incompleteness does not make it a reasonless exception under the exact definition.","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/special-pleading/","context":"Collins argues that beginning-and-end demands generating an infinite regress for temporal beings do not apply in the same way to an extra-temporal creator."},{"moveId":"con-constant-sensitivity","label":"Appeal to authority","type":"fallacy","decision":"accepted","rationale":"Dawkins invokes the agreement of 'most physicists' to support the sweeping proposition that changing any physical constant by even a very small amount prevents cosmic structure and life, without presenting the supporting evidence or precisely establishing that consensus. The assessment identifies this broad claim as undocumented and potentially obscuring parameter-specific ranges and compensating variations. Because expert consensus is doing material work where the relevant evidence and scope are not shown, the exact definition is met.","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/appeal-to-authority/","context":"Dawkins says most physicists agree that tiny changes to the constants would prevent galaxies, stars, chemistry, and ultimately the prerequisites for life."},{"moveId":"con-fine-tuner-does-not-explain","label":"Begging the question","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Dawkins's assertion that a fine-tuner explains nothing presupposes a contested explanatory standard and is overstated, but it does not directly or indirectly restate that identical conclusion as a premise. The assessment says personal explanation may provide some explanatory gain and asks Dawkins to justify extending ordinary complexity demands to God. That is an unsupported premise and unmet burden, not demonstrated circularity.","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/begging-the-question/","context":"Dawkins argues that postulating a fine-tuner merely invents away the fine-tuning problem unless the proposed agent's own explanatory status is addressed."},{"moveId":"pro-priors-mediate-explanations","label":"Confirmation bias","type":"bias","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Collins correctly observes that priors affect comparisons between underdetermined hypotheses, but he does not selectively search for, interpret, or suppress particular evidence to protect his own view in this move. The assessment says his unspecified priors, likelihoods, and complexity measures leave the result vulnerable to starting commitments. Vulnerability to bias and an incomplete Bayesian comparison do not establish confirmation bias itself.","url":"https://cogbias.site/biases/confirmation-bias/","context":"Collins compares creator and multiverse explanations, invokes Occam's razor, and says their relative plausibility partly depends on one's prior probability for God."},{"moveId":"con-multiverse-not-ad-hoc","label":"Appeal to authority","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Dawkins refers secondhand to reputable inflationary physics, but he uses its alleged independent theoretical provenance as a defeasible reason that the multiverse was not invented solely for fine-tuning. He repeatedly qualifies his expertise and admits possible error rather than treating prestige as decisive. The assessment demands model-specific substantiation, identifying underdevelopment rather than authority functioning as settlement.","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/appeal-to-authority/","context":"Dawkins tentatively recalls that multiverse proposals arise from independently motivated inflationary physics and concedes that he may have the technical relationship wrong."},{"moveId":"pro-human-capacities-fit-purpose","label":"Confirmation bias","type":"bias","decision":"accepted","rationale":"Collins declares that the universe has 'exactly' the properties expected under divine purpose while selecting morality, love, beauty, and religious seeking and omitting substantial contrary data. The assessment specifically lists parasites, disasters, disease, extinction, moral failure, and rival natural explanations as excluded from this comparison. This is material one-sided interpretation favoring an existing theistic view and therefore directly satisfies confirmation bias.","url":"https://cogbias.site/biases/confirmation-bias/","context":"Collins presents human moral responsibility, love, aesthetic appreciation, knowledge of good and evil, and religious seeking as expected products of intentional creation."},{"moveId":"pro-lawful-creation-entails-harms","label":"Scope neglect","type":"bias","decision":"accepted","rationale":"Collins moves from the general proposition that stable, generative laws can have harmful byproducts to accepting the actual natural harms without proportionately addressing their scale, frequency, severity, or distribution. The assessment expressly says he has not shown that these particular harms or their magnitude are necessary for lawfulness and desired goods. That omission materially matches failure to adjust judgment to scope.","url":"https://cogbias.site/biases/scope-neglect/","context":"Collins argues that lawful evolutionary creation inevitably produces harmful outcomes alongside beauty and that God therefore cannot intervene continually to prevent every byproduct."},{"moveId":"pro-rare-miracles-convey-message","label":"Special pleading","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Collins supplies a stated distinction for exceptional intervention: rare miracles communicate pivotal divine messages while ordinary nonintervention preserves stable natural order. The message criterion is unsupported and the assessment finds no moral explanation for prioritizing communication over rescue. Even so, it is a proposed principle rather than an exception given without any principled reason, so the exact special-pleading definition is not met.","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/special-pleading/","context":"Collins claims that a law-giving God can ordinarily preserve regularity yet make extreme message-bearing exceptions, offering the resurrection as an example."},{"moveId":"pro-constant-intervention-destroys-order","label":"Red herring","type":"fallacy","decision":"accepted","rationale":"The challenge concerns selective or bounded divine rescues, but Collins answers by imagining intervention at every hurricane and the chaos allegedly caused by continual suspension of natural law. That extreme scenario is related but materially less relevant and leaves the original bounded-intervention question unresolved. The assessment identifies this exact diversion and requires a threshold for limited miracles, directly satisfying the red-herring definition.","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/red-herring/","context":"Collins contrasts rare interventions at pivotal revelatory moments with the chaotic world he says would result if God intervened during every hurricane."},{"moveId":"pro-nobility-exceeds-misfiring-description","label":"Belief bias","type":"bias","decision":"accepted","rationale":"Collins treats the evolutionary account as inadequate because describing radical altruism as a misfiring feels incompatible with its recognized nobility. Yet the admirability of conduct does not determine whether the proposed natural causal explanation follows. The assessment expressly identifies this mistaken opposition between moral significance and causal history, showing that the appeal materially substitutes an intuitively acceptable evaluation for assessment of the inference.","url":"https://cogbias.site/biases/belief-bias/","context":"Collins says it bothers him to describe exceptionally noble sacrificial behavior as an evolutionary mechanism misfiring outside its ancestral adaptive setting."},{"moveId":"pro-morality-signposts-holy-god","label":"Argument from ignorance","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Collins frames moral obligation as a possible signpost within a cumulative case, not as proof that God exists because naturalistic accounts have not been established. His difficulty seeing obligation as purely evolutionary accompanies an incomplete positive bridge, but the assessment explicitly notes his cautious framing and treats the problem as insufficient comparison and warrant. Missing rivals and an unfinished inference alone do not meet the definition.","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/argument-from-ignorance/","context":"Collins describes felt obligation to avoid evil as resistant to a purely evolutionary account and as a possible indication of a holy God interested in persons."},{"moveId":"pro-morality-signposts-holy-god","label":"Subjective validation","type":"bias","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Collins refers to felt obligation and personal puzzlement, but he carefully presents the experience as a possible signpost rather than verification of a holy God. The assessment's limitation is that the cross-cultural evidence and inferential bridge are incomplete and naturalistic rivals insufficiently compared. It does not find that private resonance or meaningfulness is treated as establishing the claim's accuracy.","url":"https://cogbias.site/biases/subjective-validation/","context":"Collins connects the phenomenology of being obligated to avoid evil with his personal search for signs of divine holiness and relational interest."},{"moveId":"con-moral-terms-need-no-spirit","label":"Begging the question","type":"fallacy","decision":"accepted","rationale":"Defining good as what good people do and evil as what bad people do presupposes the moral classifications that the proposed account needs to establish. No independent criterion identifies who counts as good or bad, so the conclusion is embedded in the defining premises. The assessment explicitly calls the formulation circular and identifies the absence of a noncircular normative standard, making the defect material.","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/begging-the-question/","context":"Dawkins proposes that moral language can describe what good and bad people do without positing God or an independently existing moral spirit."},{"moveId":"pro-beauty-lacks-obvious-fitness-value","label":"Argument from ignorance","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Collins uses the absence of an obvious direct fitness benefit to challenge the coverage of Dawkins's narrow peahen analogy, not to establish God or conclusively falsify every natural account. The assessment lists unexamined natural alternatives and says no affirmative bridge to God is supplied. Those are material limits of comparison and warrant, but they do not show a claim treated as true merely because it remains undisproved.","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/argument-from-ignorance/","context":"Collins cites beauty in mathematics, music, and sunsets as deeply significant phenomena lacking an obvious direct evolutionary benefit and broader than mate preference."},{"moveId":"con-beauty-has-natural-analogy","label":"Equivocation","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Dawkins's analogy extends a narrow instance of aesthetic preference in peahens to the much broader range of human aesthetics, but it does not clearly shift the meaning of 'beauty' between inferential steps. The assessment chiefly identifies limited coverage and asks for a shared explanatory principle, only warning of potentially loose usage. A weak or overextended analogy is not independently enough to establish exact equivocation.","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/equivocation/","context":"Dawkins uses peahen mate preference as an example showing that a sense of beauty can arise naturally while remaining wonderful and explanation-worthy."},{"moveId":"pro-joy-suggests-transcendence","label":"Subjective validation","type":"bias","decision":"accepted","rationale":"Collins treats a fleeting, personally compelling feeling that there is 'something more' as a significant experiential contribution suggesting transcendence. The assessment directly states that this seeming does not verify a transcendent object and warns against relying on intensity or personal meaning alone. Because private resonance materially supports the claim's perceived significance despite lacking discriminating evidence, the exact bias is instantiated.","url":"https://cogbias.site/biases/subjective-validation/","context":"Collins describes Lewisian joy as a transient experience of being lifted beyond ordinary life and resists dismissing that felt glimpse as merely neurotransmission."}]}
